of the _student's_ proposal
They can help to sort things, but the quality of the student proposal

started to discuss other boundary conditions.

besides you who did express the opinion that the project was

messages.author: 7a5c2ea68524e713
messages.subject: Re: paper about GSoC 2011
parts:
GSoC11 is now finished, but it appears that there is still ongoing
discussion about a project that the majority of mentors felt was
scientifically unsound.
This is NOT a message to further one side or the other of that issue,
but to point out that Google is funding code, not scientific investigations.

It is the main job of "project" (i.e., R GSoC) admins to administer, not
to make the scientific decisions. I would not, as admin, oppose a
project where I held the minority view. Whether the majority is right or
wrong will be revealed by future developments. Much of my own work was
ignored by the computational community for many years as it was not
mainstream -- now optim() seems to get more use than even I would like.
However, in trying to play referee and bring decision-making to a
conclusion on a very tight deadline, Claudia Beleites and I received
some criticisms and commentary we felt were abusive.

I propose that any further discussion of the merit or not of project
ideas for an activity that is now historical should cease on this list,
with the sanction being that the list will be appropriately edited
otherwise.

Time for GSoC12.

John Nash
